description: Extended by every altrichq repository. Repository configs should stay thin: a base branch, a manager selection, and anything genuinely repo-specific. Everything shared belongs here so a policy change is one commit, not four.
The rule this file exists to enforce: Renovate opens and refreshes pull requests. It never merges one. Release branches are Eli's.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Refresh transitive dependencies once a week rather than never. Monday inside the maintenance window, so it lands before the week starts rather than mid-afternoon.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: The one thing allowed out of the maintenance window. A CVE fix waiting until 2am tomorrow for politeness is not politeness. It is still a PR: urgent means surfaced now, never merged now.

packageRules.description: Nothing merges itself, anywhere, under any match. Restated as the first rule so a later rule cannot quietly re-enable it -- Renovate applies packageRules in order and the last match wins, which makes an automerge added below this line effective. Do not add one.

Majors never open a PR on their own. They land on the dependency dashboard and wait for a human to tick the box. A major is a migration wearing a version number, and four of them arriving as PRs in one morning is how a dependency bot gets muted.
Everything low-risk in one PR a week. Patch and minor on ordinary packages carry little enough risk individually that reviewing them one at a time costs more attention than it saves.
0.x is not semver in practice. A 0.x minor is a breaking change often enough that grouping it with patches hides it.
Runtime and framework. Its own PR, never grouped, because a rollback needs to be one revert. Next and React move the whole rendering path; Nest moves the whole backend.
Database and cache clients. A driver change can be silently wrong rather than loudly broken -- wrong pool behaviour, a changed default isolation level -- so these get read individually.
Workflow engine. Temporal versions the server and the SDK together; a mismatched pair fails at task-queue level rather than at build.
Authentication and anything holding a credential or a token. Read every line of these. A silent behaviour change here is a security incident, not a bug.
Time. Altric schedules posts, so a timezone or DST change is a product bug that only appears at the wrong hour in the wrong month. Calendar makes this worse, not better.

Calendar and identity providers. Google and Microsoft deprecate on their own schedule and the failure is a 400 from an API, not a failed build. Named here ahead of the Calendar service existing so it inherits the rule rather than rediscovering it.
Money. A payment library changing behaviour costs real naira and the evidence arrives from a customer, not from CI.
Social platform SDKs. The scheduling product is only as correct as these, and a provider breaking change shows up as a post that silently never left.
Container base images and Kubernetes tooling. These change what runs in production rather than what is built, so they are read one at a time regardless of semver distance.

GitHub Actions. Patch and minor group; majors go to the dashboard with everything else. Tags rather than digests, deliberately -- the org pins on tags today and switching to digests would rewrite every workflow every week for a threat model nobody has agreed to.
Blacksmith's runner actions are tied to the runner images this org builds on. Never grouped, so a CI failure traces to one line.

prBodyNotes: **This PR does not merge itself.** Renovate has no automerge anywhere in the Altric organization, and no release branch accepts a bot merge. A green CI result here means the change builds, not that it ships.
Release branches (`altric` in altrichq/altric, `main` in altrichq/homepage) are merged by a human, deliberately.
